title: Limits of accuracy
summary: A [[rounding|rounded]] measurement hides its true value somewhere in a small range. The ends of that range are the [[lower-bound|lower bound]] and the [[upper-bound|upper bound]]. You'll find them for any accuracy and write them as an inequality.

goals.text: Write down the upper and lower bounds of a value rounded to the nearest unit, 5, 10 or 20.
Find the bounds of a value given to [[decimal-place|decimal places]] or [[significant-figure|significant figures]], including in a different unit.
Write the bounds as an inequality, with $\le$ and $<$ in the right places.
Choose the right bound of each value to find the upper or lower bound of a calculation.
Work out bounds for perimeters, areas and speeds found from rounded measurements.

before.hint: Look at the second decimal digit: is it $5$ or more?
before.explain: The next digit is $7$, so round the $3$ up to $4$. Revise it in {{lesson:1.9}}.

before.hint: Keep the first two digits, then fill the rest of the places with zeros.
before.explain: The third digit is $8$, so $52$ rounds up to $53$. Fill with zeros: $5300$. Revise it in {{lesson:1.9}}.

blocks.text: A pencil is $14$ cm long, to the nearest centimetre. Its real length could be $13.8$ cm, or $14.3$ cm. Any length from $13.5$ cm up to just below $14.5$ cm [[rounding|rounds]] to $14$ cm.

blocks.statement: The [[lower-bound|lower bound]] of a rounded value is the smallest value that rounds to it. The [[upper-bound|upper bound]] is where values start to round up to the next value instead.
blocks.plain: The two ends of the range the true value lies in.

blocks.text: 1. Find the rounding unit: the "nearest …" in the question. For the pencil it is $1$ cm.
2. Halve it. Half of $1$ cm is $0.5$ cm.
3. Subtract the half for the lower bound and add it for the upper bound: $14 - 0.5 = 13.5$ and $14 + 0.5 = 14.5$.

blocks.alt: Number line from 13 to 15 centimetres. The part from 13.5 to 14.5 is shaded, with 14 in the middle. 13.5 has a filled dot, labelled lower bound. 14.5 has an open dot, labelled upper bound. Below the line: 13.5 is less than or equal to l, which is less than 14.5.
blocks.caption: Every length in the shaded part rounds to $14$ cm.

blocks.text: A length of exactly $13.5$ cm rounds up to $14$ cm, so it is allowed: use $\le$. A length of exactly $14.5$ cm rounds up to $15$ cm, so it is not: use $<$. We still call $14.5$ the upper bound.

blocks.question: The length of the pencil is $l$ cm. It is $14$ cm, correct to the nearest centimetre. Write the bounds of $l$ as an inequality.
steps: The unit is $1$ cm, so half the unit is $0.5$ cm.
Lower bound: $14 - 0.5 = 13.5$. It is allowed, so use $\le$.
Upper bound: $14 + 0.5 = 14.5$. It rounds to $15$, so use $<$.

blocks.question: A parcel has a mass of $m$ grams. It is $340$ g, correct to the nearest $10$ g. Write the bounds of $m$ as an inequality.
steps: The unit is $10$ g, so half the unit is $5$ g.
Lower bound: $340 - 5 = 335$.
Upper bound: $340 + 5 = 345$. A mass of $345$ g rounds to $350$ g, so use $<$.
Check: $335$ and $344.9$ both round to $340$ to the nearest $10$.

blocks.text: Adding and subtracting the whole unit, giving $330 \le m < 350$. Always use half the unit: the value is the middle of its range.

blocks.prompt: A river is $70$ km long, correct to the nearest $5$ km. Write down the upper bound of its length, in km.
blocks.explain: $70 + 2.5 = 72.5$ km. The length is less than this, but $72.5$ is still the upper bound.

blocks.prompt: A field is $w$ metres wide. It is $260$ m, correct to the nearest $20$ m. Which inequality is right?
blocks.hint: Half of $20$ is $10$. The smaller bound goes on the left.
blocks.explain: $260 - 10 = 250$ and $260 + 10 = 270$. The others use the whole $20$ m, half of $10$ m, or half of $1$ m.

sections.heading: Decimal places, significant figures and units

blocks.text: The same three steps work for any accuracy. Only step 1 changes: the unit is the place value of the last digit that was kept.
To 1 [[decimal-place|decimal place]], the unit is $0.1$, so half is $0.05$. To 2 decimal places, the unit is $0.01$, so half is $0.005$.

For [[significant-figure|significant figures]], count along to the last significant figure and read its place value. In $2.40$ to 3 s.f., the last figure is the $0$ in the hundredths place, so the unit is $0.01$.

blocks.question: A melon has a mass of $m$ kg. It is $3.6$ kg, correct to 1 decimal place. Write the bounds of $m$ as an inequality.
steps: 1 decimal place means the unit is $0.1$ kg. Half of it is $0.05$ kg.
Upper bound: $3.6 + 0.05 = 3.65$, which rounds up to $3.7$, so use $<$.

blocks.question: A jug holds $V$ litres of juice. It is $2.40$ litres, correct to 3 significant figures. Write the bounds of $V$ as an inequality.
steps: The significant figures are $2$, $4$ and $0$. The last one is in the hundredths place, so the unit is $0.01$.

blocks.text: Ignoring a final zero. $2.40$ to 3 s.f. has a unit of $0.01$, not $0.1$, so its bounds are $2.395$ and $2.405$.
When the accuracy is in a different unit from the value, change units first. For example, $5$ cm is $0.05$ m, so half of it is $0.025$ m.

blocks.prompt: A plank is $2.8$ m long, correct to the nearest $5$ cm. Write down the upper bound of its length, in metres.
blocks.hint: Half of $5$ cm is $2.5$ cm. Divide by $100$ to change it to metres.
blocks.explain: $2.5$ cm $= 0.025$ m, so the upper bound is $2.8 + 0.025 = 2.825$ m. Adding $0.05$ m would use the whole $5$ cm.

blocks.prompt: A path is $0.38$ km long, correct to 2 significant figures. What is the lower bound of its length, in km?
blocks.hint: The last significant figure, $8$, is in the hundredths place.
blocks.explain: The unit is $0.01$, so half is $0.005$: $0.38 - 0.005 = 0.375$. $0.385$ is the upper bound.

blocks.text: When rounded values go into a calculation, the answer has bounds too. To get the biggest possible answer, pick the bound of each value that pushes the answer up.
Adding or multiplying bigger positive numbers gives a bigger answer. So the upper bound of $a + b$ or $a \times b$ uses both upper bounds.
Subtracting or dividing by a smaller number gives a bigger answer. So the upper bound of $a - b$ or $a \div b$ uses the upper bound of $a$ and the lower bound of $b$.

blocks.statement: For positive values $a$ and $b$, the upper bound of $a + b$ is $a_{\text{upper}} + b_{\text{upper}}$, of $a \times b$ is $a_{\text{upper}} \times b_{\text{upper}}$, of $a - b$ is $a_{\text{upper}} - b_{\text{lower}}$, and of $a \div b$ is $a_{\text{upper}} \div b_{\text{lower}}$. For each lower bound, swap every upper and lower.
blocks.why: Taking away less, or sharing between fewer, leaves more.

blocks.text: A value that is exact, such as a count or "exactly $3$ hours", has no bounds. Use it as it is.

blocks.question: A rectangular tile measures $23$ cm by $15$ cm, each correct to the nearest centimetre. Work out the upper bound of its area.
steps: Upper bounds of the sides: $23 + 0.5 = 23.5$ cm and $15 + 0.5 = 15.5$ cm.
Area is a product, so multiply the two upper bounds: $23.5 \times 15.5$.
Without a calculator: $23.5 \times 15 = 352.5$ and $23.5 \times 0.5 = 11.75$.
Add: $352.5 + 11.75 = 364.25$. This is exact, so do not round it.

check.prompt: Work out the upper bound of the same tile's perimeter, in cm.
check.hint: Perimeter is a sum, so use both upper bounds, twice each.

blocks.question: A car travels $150$ km, correct to the nearest $10$ km. The journey takes $2.5$ hours, correct to the nearest $0.1$ hour. Work out the lower bound of its average speed. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
steps: Speed $= \dfrac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}$, a division. For the smallest speed, use the shortest distance and the longest time.
Lower bound of distance: $150 - 5 = 145$ km.
Upper bound of time: $2.5 + 0.05 = 2.55$ hours.
Write the calculation first: $\dfrac{145}{2.55} = 56.862\ldots$ km/h.
Round only at the end: $56.9$ km/h to 3 s.f.

blocks.text: Dividing upper bound by upper bound. For the biggest quotient, divide by the lower bound; for the smallest, divide by the upper bound.
For a bounds calculation, write the bounds you use, such as $\frac{145}{2.55}$, before the answer. That line earns the method mark. Leave an exact answer such as $364.25$ unrounded.

blocks.prompt: A ribbon is $9.4$ m long. A piece $3.7$ m long is cut off. Both lengths are correct to 1 decimal place. What is the upper bound of the length left, in metres?
blocks.hint: Take the longest ribbon and cut off the shortest piece.
blocks.explain: $9.45 - 3.65 = 5.8$ m. Using $9.45 - 3.75$ gives $5.7$, which is too small.

blocks.prompt: $p = 30$, correct to the nearest $10$, and $q = 8$, correct to the nearest whole number. Work out the upper bound of $\frac{p}{q}$. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
blocks.hint: Use the upper bound of $p$ and the lower bound of $q$.

blocks.text: Halve the rounding unit. Lower bound $=$ value $-$ half the unit. Upper bound $=$ value $+$ half the unit.
For decimal places and significant figures, the unit is the place value of the last digit kept: 1 d.p. means $0.1$, and $2.40$ to 3 s.f. means $0.01$. Change units before you halve.
For positive values: upper bound of $a + b$ or $a \times b$ uses both upper bounds. Upper bound of $a - b$ or $a \div b$ uses upper $a$ and lower $b$. Swap them all for the lower bound.
Exact values have no bounds. Round only the final answer.

mistakes: Adding and subtracting the whole rounding unit. For the nearest $10$ g, the bounds are $5$ g either side, not $10$ g.
Writing the bounds the wrong way round. The lower bound goes on the left, before $\le$; the upper bound goes after $<$.
Getting the units wrong. Half of $10$ cm is $5$ cm, which is $0.05$ m, not $0.1$ m.
examTips: Write down the bounds: no working is needed, but each correct bound earns its own mark. Put them in the order $\text{lower} \le x < \text{upper}$.
Check each bound by rounding it: the lower bound must round to the given value, and the upper bound must round up to the next one.
